channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: U.S. Senate expected to confirm Jay Clayton as next Intelligence Director
item.description: Jay Claton was to be confirmed as the next intelligence director in June after Tulsi Gabbard resigned without Bill Pulte taking over, but President Trump delayed Mr. Clayton's nomination before the Senate leaving a two-week recess, allowing Mr. Pulte to take the job temporarily U. S. Senate expected to confirm Jay Clayton as next Intelligence Director.

item.title: Company fired woman during probation but fails to prove poor performance, to pay her S$30,000 for
item.description: The tribunal found that the woman was assessed by a standard which was not made obvious or clear to her, and there was a mismatch between what the woman considered the substance of her role and what her supervisor valued. Company fired woman during probation but fails to prove poor performance, to pay her S$30,000 for.

item.title: Extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
item.description: From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown“It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan. The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains.

item.title: Iran War Drives Central Asian Countries To Seek Alternate Trade Routes
item.description: In an interview with RFE/RL, Ken Moriyasu, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, said the countries of Central Asia appear to be giving up on Iran as a gateway to global trade, a situation which is driving new approaches to cooperation with China and Pakistan. Iran War Drives Central Asian Countries To Seek Alternate Trade Routes.

item.title: Central Asia Is Increasingly Looking Beyond Iran, Says Analyst Ken Moriyasu
item.description: Has the Iran conflict permanently reshaped Central Asia's strategic map? Hudson Institute senior fellow Ken Moriyasu explains why governments across the region are increasingly looking beyond Iran toward Pakistan, Afghanistan and China for trade, connectivity, and access to global markets. Central Asia Is Increasingly Looking Beyond Iran, Says Analyst Ken Moriyasu.

item.title: Pinochet-era soldier jailed for killing folk singer Víctor Jara 53 years ago
item.description: Nelson Haase Mazzei was sentenced for murdering Víctor Jara in 2023, but fled from authorities in ChileMore than 50 years after the murder of the Chilean folk singer Víctor Jara, the last man wanted in connection with his death has been tracked down and brought to justice. item.title: 60-Year-Old Ukrainian Volunteer Supplies Front Lines Amid Rise Of Unmanned Ground Vehicles
item.description: Russian drone attacks are making it increasingly dangerous to deliver supplies to Ukraine's frontline troops. While Kyiv is deploying unmanned ground vehicles for some risky missions, volunteers like 60-year-old Mykhaylo continue making supply runs the old-fashioned way in the Donetsk region. 60-Year-Old Ukrainian Volunteer Supplies Front Lines Amid Rise Of Unmanned Ground Vehicles.

item.title: High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution
item.description: The AIDS epidemic could stage a comeback amid unequal access to breakthrough prevention medicines and a sharp decline in global funding, according to a UN report released on Monday ahead of the opening of the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. High prices and funding cuts stall HIV prevention revolution.

item.title: Bank Indonesia chief’s resignation signals a deep, hidden crisis
item.description: JAKARTA – Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo’s abrupt resignation marks a watershed moment for Southeast Asia’s largest economy. Coming midway through his second five-year term, Warjiyo’s departure. tendered for personal reasons and quickly accepted by President Prabowo Subianto. has rattled local and international financial markets. item.description: Modern terrorist attacks no longer end when the shooting stops. Increasingly, a second battle begins immediately afterward: the struggle over who receives credit. In an era of encrypted communications, instant messaging and digital propaganda, attaching an organization’s name to an attack can be almost as valuable as the hit itself. item.title: Uganda begins emergency food handouts after 19 die from hunger
item.description: Government move follows months of drought and crop failures in Karamoja, with 1.5m people facing malnutritionUganda has launched emergency food relief distribution after at least 19 deaths from hunger were reported in an area of prolonged drought in the east of the country. Uganda begins emergency food handouts after 19 die from hunger.

item.description: China’s latest sea-based rocket launch shows how mobile launch platforms, onboard artificial intelligence and expanding commercial constellations are converging into a broader Chinese effort to strengthen military resilience, accelerate satellite deployment and compete for economic influence across an increasingly contested orbital domain. item.title: Zelenskyy Becomes First Foreign Visitor For New British PM Burnham
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is set to meet new British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in London on July 27 as he begins a big week of foreign talks amid a rising civilian death toll from Russian air strikes back home. Ukrainian Leader To Kick Off Big Week With London Meeting With New British PM. Zelenskyy To Kick Off Big Week With London Meeting With New British PM.

item.title: Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail
item.description: Exclusive: CSI Aviation and GlobalX accused of violating civil rights as part of Trump immigration crackdownVenezuelan men sent last year to a notorious Salvadorian terrorism prison by the Trump administration are suing the US aviation companies that transported them there. Venezuela men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail. Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail.

item.title: Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN
item.description: When Samantha Richards and Angela Hifume walked into the Hall of Flags at United Nations Headquarters last week, they carried more than a folder of paper. They carried the voices of hundreds of street-connected children who had never expected anyone to listen. Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN.

item.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
item.description: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country. UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime.

item.title: Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan
item.description: China's investments in Pakistan's Balochistan are increasingly at risk as attacks by separatists are on the rise in the impoverished region. The worsening security situation has strained ties between the Iron Brothers, raising concerns over the future of Beijing's investments in Pakistan. Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan.

item.title: Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region
item.description: US President Donald ⁠Trump ⁠said Washington and Tehran were still conducting negotiations to end their conflict -- even as attacks intensified throughout the region, further threatening to widen the conflict into a full-blown Middle East war. Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region.

item.title: Russia's 'Axis Of Upheaval' Is Built To Last Beyond Ukraine, Analyst Kendall-Taylor Says
item.description: Russia's deepening partnerships with China, Iran, and North Korea represent one of the most significant geopolitical realignments driven by the war in Ukraine. Yet according to Andrea Kendall-Taylor, viewing this grouping through the lens of a traditional military alliance misses the bigger picture. Russia's 'Axis Of Upheaval' Is Built To Last Beyond Ukraine, Analyst Kendall-Taylor Says.
